items.headline: Flood Watch issued August 5 at 4:22AM AKDT until August 5 at 2:00PM AKDT by NWS Anchorage AK
items.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...The following area, Central Susitna Valley.  This includes
the cities of Talkeetna, Trapper Creek, And Petersville.

* WHEN...Until 2 PM AKDT this afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Additional rainfall up to 0.5 inches is possible along the
Susitna and Chulitna Basins through Wednesda
items.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be alert for possible Flood
Warnings. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be prepared
to take action should flooding develop.

Stay tuned to further developments by listening to your local radio,
television, or NOAA Weather Radio for further informat

items.headline: Flood Warning issued August 5 at 4:18AM AKDT until August 5 at 5:00PM AKDT by NWS Anchorage AK
items.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Petersville Area

* WHEN...Until 500 PM AKDT Wednesday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations is imminent or occurring. Low-water
crossings are inundated with water and may not be passable.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 359 AM AKDT, Doppler radar and automated rain gauges
indicated scattered rain showers continue across the warned
area. Flooding is ongoing or expected
items.instruction:
Stay tuned to further developments by listening to your local radio,
television, or NOAA Weather Radio for further information.

deaths occur in vehicles.

items.headline: Flood Warning issued August 5 at 4:18AM AKDT until August 7 at 1:00PM AKDT by NWS Anchorage AK
items.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues.

* WHERE...Yentna River including Lake Creek.

* WHEN...Until 100 PM AKDT Friday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations is imminent or occurring. Streams
continue to rise due to excess runoff from earlier rainfall.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
